title: Equivalent fractions, simplest form, mixed numbers and improper fractions
blurb: Build equivalent fractions, switch between mixed numbers and improper fractions, and give every answer in the form asked: lowest terms or a mixed number.
question: A resident's juice intake is charted as 11/4 cups, and a menu card lists a portion as 6/8 cup. How do you write the intake as a mixed number and the portion in lowest terms?

teach.h: Three ways to write a fraction
teach.body: Formally, a proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator (3/4), an improper fraction has a numerator equal to or greater than its denominator (11/4), and a mixed number is a whole number plus a proper fraction (2 3/4). In plain English: an improper fraction and a mixed number can be the same amount written two ways. You need mixed numbers for answers and improper fractions for multiplying and dividing.

items: Mixed → improper, 3 2/5: whole × denominator + numerator = 3 × 5 + 2 = 17. Keep the denominator: 17/5.
Improper → mixed, 29/6: 29 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 5. Quotient is the whole number, remainder over the same denominator: 4 5/6.

teach.caption: Going back: divide 17 by 5. The quotient (3) is the whole; the remainder (2) goes over 5.

teach.body: Multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number gives an equivalent fraction: 3/4 = 6/8 = 9/12. To fill in a missing term, find what the known term was multiplied by and do the same to the other: 3/4 = ?/28 is ×7, so 21/28. A fraction is in lowest terms when top and bottom share no factor except 1: divide both by the greatest common factor (GCF). Adding the same number to top and bottom does NOT keep the value.

teach.h: Format drills: give the form the stem asks for
items: "In lowest terms": 42/56. GCF 14 → 3/4. The option 21/28 is equal but wrong, because 21 and 28 still share 7.
"As a mixed number": 23/4. 23 ÷ 4 = 5 remainder 3 → 5 3/4. The option 23/4 is equal but in the wrong form.
"As a mixed number in lowest terms": 46/8 → 5 6/8 → 5 3/4. Divide first, then simplify the fraction part.
"As an improper fraction in lowest terms": 3 6/9 → 33/9 → 11/3. Check: 11 ÷ 3 = 3 remainder 2, and 3 2/3 = 3 6/9. ✓

head: Number
Factors
teach.caption: Dividing by a smaller shared factor (such as 2) is fine, but repeat until no factor is shared.

steps.sub: do the same to the numerator

teach.caption: Never add: 5 + 48 over 8 + 48 gives 53/56, a different value.

teach.text: Slips the HESI A2 turns into options: reading 2 3/4 as 23/4; multiplying the whole by the numerator (3 2/5 → 11/5); forgetting to add the numerator (3 2/5 → 15/5); and, when the stem says "lowest terms", an equal but unsimplified fraction (21/28 for 3/4). An equal value in the wrong form is a wrong answer.

teach.h: Scenario: Aisha charts a resident's fluids
teach.body: Aisha Bello, a nursing applicant volunteering in a long-term care facility, sees juice intake of 11/4 cups. 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3, so she writes 2 3/4 cups (check: 2 × 4 + 3 = 11). The menu card says 6/8 cup per portion. The GCF of 6 and 8 is 2, so the portion is 3/4 cup (check: 3 × 2 = 6, 4 × 2 = 8).

items: Mixed → improper: whole × denominator + numerator, over the same denominator.
Improper → mixed: divide; quotient = whole number, remainder over the denominator.
Lowest terms: divide top and bottom by the GCF, and check no factor is still shared.
Equivalent fractions come from multiplying or dividing top and bottom by the same number, never adding.
Read the answer form in the stem: lowest terms, mixed number or improper fraction.

summary: You can now build equivalent fractions, convert between mixed numbers and improper fractions in both directions, and reduce any fraction to lowest terms with the greatest common factor. You give each answer in the form the stem asks for and spot the digit-reading and missing-step slips the HESI A2 uses as distractors.

A.q: Which fraction with a denominator of 56 is equivalent to 3/8?
A.why: 56 ÷ 8 = 7, so multiply the numerator by 7 too: 3 × 7 = 21, giving 21/56. Check: 21/56 simplifies by 7 to 3/8.

whyNot.0: 24/56 multiplies the numerator by 8, the old denominator, instead of by 7.
whyNot.2: 51/56 adds 48 to the top and the bottom; adding the same number changes the value.
whyNot.3: 10/56 adds the multiplier 7 to the numerator (3 + 7) instead of multiplying by it.

A.q: Over one day, a toddler drinks 27/4 cups of formula. Which mixed number is equal to 27/4?

whyNot.1: 7 1/4 = 29/4: the quotient is too big, since 7 × 4 = 28 is more than 27.
whyNot.3: 7 3/4 = 31/4: both the quotient and the value are too big.

A.q: A nursing student answered 48 of 60 practice questions correctly. What fraction of the questions, in lowest terms, did she answer correctly?
A.why: The GCF of 48 and 60 is 12: 48 ÷ 12 = 4 and 60 ÷ 12 = 5, giving 4/5. Check: 4/5 = 0.8 and 48 ÷ 60 = 0.8.

whyNot.0: 24/30 is equivalent but not in lowest terms: 24 and 30 still share a factor of 6.
whyNot.2: 8/10 is equivalent but not in lowest terms: 8 and 10 still share a factor of 2.
whyNot.3: 4/6 divides 48 by 12 but 60 by 10. Dividing top and bottom by different numbers changes the value.

B.why: 15/35 simplifies by 5 to 3/7, and 6/14 also simplifies by 2 to 3/7. Check: 15 × 14 = 210 and 35 × 6 = 210.

whyNot.0: 20/40 adds 5 to the top and bottom; adding does not keep the value (20/40 = 1/2).
whyNot.1: 10/30 subtracts 5 from the top and bottom, giving 1/3, a different value.
whyNot.2: 5/7 divides the top by 3 but the bottom by 5. Both must be divided by the same number.

B.q: Which value is NOT equal to 2 2/3?
B.why: 2 2/3 = (2 × 3 + 2)/3 = 8/3. 22/3 = 7 1/3, which reads the digits 2 and 2 as the number 22.

B.q: A dietitian's soup recipe calls for 46/8 cups of broth. What is 46/8 as a mixed number in simplest form?
B.why: 46 ÷ 8 = 5 remainder 6, so 5 6/8. Simplify 6/8 by the GCF 2: 5 3/4. Check: 5 × 4 + 3 = 23 and 23/4 = 46/8.

whyNot.1: 5 6/8 is equal in value but the fraction part is not simplified (6 and 8 share 2).
whyNot.2: 6 3/4 = 27/4 = 54/8: the quotient is 5, not 6, because 6 × 8 = 48 is more than 46.
whyNot.3: 5 3/8 halves the numerator but not the denominator, which changes the value.

C.q: Write 70/12 as a mixed number in lowest terms.

whyNot.0: 5 10/12 has the right value, but the stem asks for lowest terms and 10 and 12 still share 2.
whyNot.2: 5 5/12 halves the numerator but not the denominator, which changes the value.
whyNot.3: 6 5/6 = 41/6 = 82/12: the quotient is 5, because 6 × 12 = 72 is more than 70.

C.q: A pharmacist has 3 bottles, each holding 2 2/3 ounces of cough syrup. Each dose is 1/3 ounce. How many full doses are in the 3 bottles altogether?
C.why: 2 2/3 = 8/3, which is 8 thirds of an ounce per bottle. 3 bottles × 8 thirds = 24 thirds = 24 doses. Check: 24 × 1/3 = 8 ounces = 3 × 2 2/3.

whyNot.0: 8 is the total in ounces (3 × 8/3 = 8), an intermediate answer; the question asks for 1/3-ounce doses.
whyNot.1: 21 comes from converting 2 2/3 as (2 × 2 + 3)/3 = 7/3 instead of 8/3.
whyNot.2: 12 comes from converting 2 2/3 as (2 + 2)/3 = 4/3 instead of 8/3.

C.q: A unit has 48 beds and 36 are occupied. Which gives the occupied fraction in lowest terms and the GCF used to get it?

whyNot.1: 6 is a common factor but not the greatest; 6/8 still shares a factor of 2.
whyNot.2: 4 is a common factor but not the greatest; 9/12 still shares a factor of 3.
whyNot.3: 4/3 is the fraction upside down (48/36): it compares all beds to occupied beds.

reteach.title: Think in pizza slices
reteach.question: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices, and a party has 19 slices on the table. How do you say that as whole pizzas plus slices, and why can 4 slices also be called half a pizza?

blocks.body: 19/8 means 19 slices when 8 slices make a pizza. Box them up: 8 slices fill one box, 16 fill two, and 3 are left over. So 19/8 = 2 3/8 pizzas. Going the other way, 2 3/8 pizzas is 2 × 8 = 16 slices plus 3 more: 19 slices, 19/8. Simplifying is just using bigger slices: 4 of 8 slices is the same food as 1 of 2 halves.

items: 4/8 of a pizza: cut it into halves instead and it is 1/2. Divide top and bottom by 4.
6/8 of a pizza: cut it into quarters instead and it is 3/4. Divide top and bottom by 2.
The amount of pizza never changes, only the size of each slice.

blocks.text: 2 3/8 is not 23 slices. The 2 counts whole pizzas, worth 8 slices each.

explain.body: Proper: numerator smaller than denominator, so less than 1. Improper: numerator equal to or larger than denominator, so 1 or more. Mixed number: a whole number with a proper fraction beside it.

test.q: Which of these is an improper fraction?
test.why: In 9/8 the numerator (9) is greater than the denominator (8), so it is improper. It equals 1 1/8.

whyNot.0: 8/9 has a smaller numerator than denominator, so it is proper.
whyNot.1: 1 1/8 has the same value as 9/8, but it is written as a mixed number, not an improper fraction.
whyNot.3: 7/9 has a smaller numerator than denominator, so it is proper.

explain.body: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and keep the denominator. 5 3/8: 5 × 8 = 40 eighths, plus 3 = 43 eighths, so 43/8.

test.q: A wound measures 5 3/8 inches. Which improper fraction is equal to 5 3/8?

whyNot.1: 53/8 reads the digits 5 and 3 as the number 53.
whyNot.2: 23/8 multiplies the whole by the numerator and adds the denominator: 5 × 3 + 8.
whyNot.3: 40/8 forgets to add the numerator 3; 40/8 is exactly 5.

explain.body: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number; the remainder goes over the original denominator. 38/5: 38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3, so 7 3/5.

test.q: Which mixed number is equal to 38/5?

whyNot.3: 7 3/8 puts the remainder over 8; the denominator stays 5.

explain.body: Divide top and bottom by their greatest common factor. If you use a smaller common factor, keep going until nothing is shared. 54/72: the GCF is 18, giving 3/4.

whyNot.0: 27/36 divides by 2 only; 27 and 36 still share 9.
whyNot.1: 9/12 divides by 6 only; 9 and 12 still share 3.
whyNot.2: 2/3 = 48/72, not 54/72; top and bottom were divided by different numbers.
